\chapter{On the Way Out}
\label{ch:te-on-the-way-out}
\hlchaptermodality{90}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can tell someone to take care and to come soon, say I am going home, suggest we leave, and take my leave politely.}

Complete TE-C90-letsgo: leave a visit well.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[jāgratta]{\te{జాగ్రత్త} (jāgratta) — care, caution}

\label{lesson:TE-C90-care}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a wedding, then the Telugu for an address.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{జాగ్రత్త}}
\textbf{\te{జాగ్రత్త}} (\emph{jāgratta}) — \textquotedblleft{}care, caution\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{జాగ్రత్తగా} \te{వెళ్ళండి}} — \textquotedblleft{}go carefully\textquotedblright{}, what a host says at the door, where English says \textquotedblleft{}take care\textquotedblright{}. The \textbf{-\te{గా}} is the ending that makes a manner.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The kindest thing to say to someone leaving.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāgratta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jāgratta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{jāgrattagā veḷḷaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a wedding, then the Telugu for an address, then say \emph{jāgratta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{జాగ్రత్త} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Care, caution\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tvaragā]{\te{త్వరగా} (tvaragā) — quickly, soon}

\label{lesson:TE-C90-soon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for an address, then the Telugu for care.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{త్వరగా}}
\textbf{\te{త్వరగా}} (\emph{tvaragā}) — \textquotedblleft{}quickly\textquotedblright{}, and at a parting, \textquotedblleft{}soon\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{త్వరగా} \te{రండి}} — \textquotedblleft{}come back soon\textquotedblright{}. The respectful \textbf{raṇḍi} you already have.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An invitation to return, built from pieces you own.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tvaragā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tvaragā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tvaragā raṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for an address, then the Telugu for care, then say \emph{tvaragā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{త్వరగా} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Quickly, soon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[iṇṭiki]{\te{ఇంటికి} (iṇṭiki) — home, to the house}

\label{lesson:TE-C90-home}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for care, then the Telugu for soon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ఇంటికి}}
\textbf{\te{ఇంటికి}} (\emph{iṇṭiki}) — \textquotedblleft{}home\textquotedblright{}, as in \textquotedblleft{}going home\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{ఇల్లు}}, \textquotedblleft{}a house\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{-\te{కి}} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} ending on it, and the house word changes shape to take it. \textbf{\te{నేను} \te{ఇంటికి} \te{వెళ్తాను}} — \textquotedblleft{}I am going home\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A reason to leave that needs no apology.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṇṭiki}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṇṭiki}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nēnu iṇṭiki veḷtānu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for care, then the Telugu for soon, then say \emph{iṇṭiki} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{ఇంటికి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Home, to the house\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[selavu]{\te{సెలవు} (selavu) — leave, a holiday}

\label{lesson:TE-C90-leave}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for soon, then the Telugu for home.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{సెలవు}}
\textbf{\te{సెలవు}} (\emph{selavu}) — \textquotedblleft{}leave\textquotedblright{}, both a holiday and permission to go.

\textbf{\te{ఇవాళ} \te{సెలవు}} — \textquotedblleft{}today is a holiday\textquotedblright{}. At a formal parting, \textbf{\te{సెలవు}} alone asks leave to go, the way English once said \textquotedblleft{}by your leave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A holiday, and the most formal way out of a room.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{selavu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{selavu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{ivāḷa selavu}, then take your leave with \emph{selavu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for soon, then the Telugu for home, then say \emph{selavu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{సెలవు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Leave, a holiday\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[padaṇḍi]{\te{పదండి} (padaṇḍi) — let's go}

\label{lesson:TE-C90-letsgo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for home, then the Telugu for leave.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పదండి}}
\textbf{\te{పదండి}} (\emph{padaṇḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}let's go\textquotedblright{}, said to the group you are leaving with.

It carries the respectful \textbf{-\te{అండి}} like \textbf{raṇḍi} and \textbf{āgaṇḍi}, so it stays polite even when it hurries people along.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Take care, come soon, I am going home, farewell, let's go: a whole exit.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{padaṇḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{padaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for home, then the Telugu for leave, then say \emph{padaṇḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{పదండి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Let's go\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
